angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 95,450,040 km at 2991.10 pc = 0.43 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, AQ Pup: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 2991.1 +/- 141.3 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 2991.1 +/- 141.3 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 0.2751 +/- 0.0226 mas (same row, RUWE 1.18), 12.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 137.2 +/- 6.6 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, AQ Pup: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 137.2 +/- 6.6 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 95,450,040 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5125 +/- 208 K from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 20, Name='AQ Pup', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5125 +/- 208 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 20, Name='AQ Pup', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5125 +/- 208 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 0.41 from 2024A&A...690A.246T, the median of its 2 spectra; the 8 published values span log g 0.2 to 1.66, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...690A.246T)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* AQ Pup: spectral type F5-G2Ib (1966AJ.....71..999F)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* AQ Pup: main object type cC*, Classical Cepheid Variable

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
